paper.title: A framework to evaluate machine learning crystal stability predictions
paper.research_summary: We present Matbench Discovery as an example evaluation framework for machine learning energy models, here applied as pre-filters to first-principles computed data in a high-throughput search for stable inorganic crystals.

tasks.objective: To accelerate high-throughput computational materials discovery by using ML models as efficient pre-filters for DFT calculations to identify thermodynamically stable inorganic crystals.
target_properties: distance to convex hull phase diagram
constraints: models must predict convex hull distance from unrelaxed structures only
avoid circular dependency with DFT relaxation

evidence.text: We present Matbench Discovery as an example evaluation framework for machine learning energy models, here applied as pre-filters to first-principles computed data in a high-throughput search for stable inorganic crystals.
Our work aims to identify the state-of-the-art model by proposing an evaluation framework that closely simulates a real-world discovery campaign guided by ML models.

stages.stage_name_raw: Acquire test data from WBM dataset
stages.stage_goal: Obtain prospectively generated unrelaxed crystal structures with corresponding DFT-relaxed formation energies for realistic out-of-distribution evaluation.
stage_output: WBM dataset of 215,488 unique protostructure unrelaxed structures with target PBE formation energies of relaxed counterparts

evidence.text: Our test set consists of the unrelaxed structures in the WBM dataset50. Their target values are the PBE formation energies of the corresponding DFT-relaxed structures.

The WBM dataset50 consists of 257,487 structures generated via chemical similarity-based elemental substitution of MP source structures followed by DFT relaxation and calculating each crystal’s convex hull distance.

stages.stage_name_raw: Clean and filter WBM test set by protostructure matching
stages.stage_goal: Remove potential data leakage between MP training set and WBM test set by eliminating structures with matching final protostructures.
stage_output: cleaned WBM unique prototype test set of 215,488 structures

evidence.text: To control for the potential adverse effects of leakage between the MP training set and the WBM test set, we cleaned the WBM test set based on protostructure matching. We refer to the combination of a materials prototype and the elemental assignment of its wyckoff positions as a protostructure following ref. 62. First we removed 524 pathological structures in WBM based on formation energies being larger than 5 eV per atom or smaller than −5 eV per atom. We then removed from the WBM test set all examples where the final protostructure of a WBM material matched the final protostructure of an MP material. In total, 11,175 materials were cleaned using this filter. We further removed all duplicated protostructures within WBM, keeping the lowest energy structure in each instance, leaving 215,488 structures in the unique prototype test set.

stages.stage_name_raw: Compute convex hull distance labels for WBM structures
stages.stage_goal: Derive thermodynamic stability labels by computing each WBM structure's distance to the convex hull of the MP training set.
stage_input: PBE formation energies of DFT-relaxed WBM structures
stage_output: convex hull distance labels (EMP hull dist ≤ 0 for stable)

evidence.text: Throughout this work, we define stability as being on or below the convex hull of the MP training set (EMP hull dist ≤ 0). In total, 32,942 of 215,488 materials in the WBM unique prototype test set satisfy this criterion.

The convex hull distance of a relaxed structure is chosen as the measure of its thermodynamic stability, rather than the formation energy, as it informs the decision on whether to pursue a potential candidate crystal.

stages.stage_name_raw: Train ML models on MP data to predict convex hull distance
stages.stage_goal: Train diverse ML models—including universal interatomic potentials, graph neural networks, and random forests—on MP data to predict convex hull distance from unrelaxed inputs.
stage_input: MP v.2022.10.28 training data (energies, forces, stresses, magnetic moments)
stage_output: trained ML models (e.g., EquiformerV2+DeNS, ORB MPtrj, SevenNet, etc.)

evidence.text: To test a wide variety of methodologies proposed for learning the potential energy landscape, our initial benchmark release includes 13 models.

We define the MP3 v.2022.10.28 database release as the maximum allowed training set for any compliant model submission. Models may train on the complete set of relaxation frames, or any subset thereof such as the final relaxed structures. Any subsets of the energies, forces and stresses are valid training targets.

stages.stage_name_raw: Evaluate models on WBM test set using classification metrics
stages.stage_goal: Assess model performance using task-relevant classification metrics (F1, DAF, precision, recall) rather than regression metrics alone.
stage_output: performance metrics (F1, DAF, precision, recall, MAE, RMSE, R2)

evidence.text: Table 1 shows performance metrics for all models included in the initial release of Matbench Discovery reported on the unique protostructure subset.
The discovery acceleration factor (DAF) quantifies how many times more effective a model is at finding stable structures compared with random selection from the test set.
Our analysis reveals that universal interatomic potentials (UIPs) surpass all other methodologies we evaluated in terms of both accuracy and robustness.

stages.stage_name_raw: Rank candidates by predicted hull distance for discovery campaigns
stages.stage_goal: Simulate prospective materials discovery by ranking WBM candidates by model-predicted hull distance and computing cumulative precision/recall.
stage_input: model-predicted hull distances for WBM test set

evidence.text: For each model, we iterate through that list and calculate at each step the precision and recall of correctly identified stable materials. This simulates exactly how these models would be used in a prospective materials discovery campaign and reveals how a model’s performance changes as a function of the discovery campaign length.
A typical discovery campaign will rank hypothetical materials by model-predicted hull distance from most to least stable and validate the most stable predictions first.
We define the MP3 v.2022.10.28 database release as the maximum allowed training set for any compliant model submission.

Our benchmark defines the training set as all data available from the v.2022.10.28 MP release. We recorded a snapshot of energies, forces, stresses and magnetic moments for all MP ionic steps on 15 March 2023 as the canonical training set for Matbench Discovery, and provide convenience functions through our Python package for easily feeding those data into future model submissions to our benchmark.

The MP is a widely used database of inorganic materials properties that have been calculated using high-throughput ab initio methods. At the time of writing, the MP database3 has grown to ~154,000 crystals, covering diverse chemistries and providing relaxed and initial structures as well as the relaxation trajectory for every entry.
